title: What I'm Buying In The Most Disconnected Market I've Seen
creator: Daniel Pronk
summary: Daniel Pronk argues the market is the most disconnected he has seen: the S&P 500 fell over 2% in the morning on a hot October PCE print (3.8%, the second-highest since April 2023) and then recovered almost all of it, while semiconductors and AI stocks sold off hard — AMD hit around $375. His core argument is that hyperscaler AI capex is paying off, and he rebuts a viral post comparing hyperscaler capex with frontier-lab revenue: Meta does not sell its compute, and its advertiser cost per acquisition is down 33%, it adds the most ad revenue per quarter versus Amazon and Google, and trailing revenue is $242bn growing 26%+ for three straight quarters. Amazon's revenue growth is accelerating (15% company-wide, AWS approaching 40%, fastest in five years) with record operating margins and its price to operating cash flow the lowest since 2010; Google Cloud grew 102% last quarter. He plays clips from Dan Ives (third year of an 8-10 year AI buildout, $3-4tn of capex ahead), Bill Ackman (the AI race is a national-security matter that cannot be slowed) and Stanley Druckenmiller (no clarity on the next 12 months, not long or short equities, short copper), plus Michael Burry covering his shorts and going long, and Dell's blowout quarter (revenue +103% to $54.9bn, $132.3bn backlog) as evidence AI demand is durable. Calls: AMZN BUY, META BUY, MELI BUY and ROAD (Construction Partners) BUY — all reiterations — as he deploys a record amount of capital, saying he is 'pretty much tapped out'. He also plugs his 40%-off Black Friday course sale, ending Monday. Note: the caption garbles MercadoLibre as 'Marcato, Libre'.

calls.video_title: What I'm Buying In The Most Disconnected Market I've Seen
calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (last BUY 24 Nov). Continuing to buy aggressively — deploying a record amount of capital in the sell-off. Amazon's price to operating cash flow is the lowest since 2010 while the business accelerates: company revenue growth 15%, AWS approaching 40% (fastest in 5 years), operating margins at all-time highs as AWS grows share of the mix. AWS capex has a ~3-year payback, then ~2 years of near-pure free cash flow; frontier AI labs are only ~7% of AWS revenue, demand is broad-based from tens of thousands of customers.
calls.base: AWS keeps compounding and the capex converts into free cash flow in the 2030s harvest phase.
calls.bull: The market recognises hyperscaler capex is paying off and multiples re-rate while growth accelerates.
calls.bear: The capex cycle suppresses free cash flow longer than expected, or AI demand slows.
calls.price_at_call: P/OCF lowest since 2010; AWS revenue growth approaching 40%

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (last BUY 24 Nov). Buying aggressively. Meta's AI capex is paying off inside its own business: advertisers are seeing a 33% decline in cost per acquisition, Meta is adding the most advertising revenue per quarter versus Amazon and Google, and trailing-12-month revenue is $242B, growing 26%+ for three straight quarters.
calls.base: AI keeps improving ad targeting and revenue keeps compounding at 25%+.
calls.bull: Ad-share gains accelerate and Meta overtakes Google as the largest digital advertiser.
calls.bear: Capex keeps rising faster than the ad payoff, or advertiser demand softens.

Construction Partners 'freaking paves roads' — a road maintenance and construction company with no AI exposure — yet it is selling off with the index, which he calls indiscriminate selling and an opportunity; he has been adding aggressively.
calls.base: Long-term contracts keep revenue compounding and the sell-off proves indiscriminate.
